```
{"A_tab":2,"H":6,"S_cells":4,"globals":{},"heap_base":32,"heap_limit_max":32,"interface_regions":{"plus_db":{"db":{"base":17}},"through":{"db":{"base":16}}},"null_size":16,"ptr_width":32}
```

The outer invocation's B is independent of `tk`'s tuple. The sole
`@worker` binding key is `[0,1,0]` (oracle argument positions 0 and 1,
region position 0). It has five locations (`x r fr zero bad`), so
R_worker = 8 cells; forwarding the three additional parameters adds no
cells. The two outer rows precede its six rows: indices 0, 1 and 2..7,
HALT = 8, P = 4. `@plus_db` has six rows and no lproc calls. The byte
region maps at 16 in the outer oracle and 17 in the nested oracle;
both mappings refer to the same passed cells, with no byte copy.

For every x, a ∈ [0,4) and byte d ∈ [0,256), an outer tuple
(B ≥ 8, 0, stack_limit ≥ 8, depth_limit ≥ 1) and `tk` tuple (6,0,0,0)
give F_B(x,d) = (((x + a + (d mod 4)) mod 4) XOR 1, 0).
For arbitrary initial target t and fault f, the final values are
(t XOR payload, f); x and d are unchanged and all workspace is clean.
This permutation extends by linearity to superpositions and an
entangled reference. With outer B = 7 the success path has not executed
`lift.retval`, so the outcome is (0, `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS`); with outer
stack_limit = 7 or depth_limit = 0 the first row gives
(0, `FAULT_BUDGET_DEPTH`). With `tk` tuple (5,0,0,0), the nested oracle
returns fault 1; the lproc's `lift.faultif` propagates code 9 at outer
step 5, so B ≥ 5 gives (0, `FAULT_CALLEE`). The nested fault, stack
history, parameters and locations are cleared by prefix reversal; no
additional charge arises from forwarding, commit or reversal.

## 17. Decisions deferred to implementation, with defaults

Each item is one an implementer must decide to build; any decision is
conformant provided two implementations agree on the default below until
the item is revised. Items 1–5 are asserted non-semantic.

1. **Binary encoding.** Default: none; §16 text is the only interchange
   form.
2. **Gate-name registry.** Default: the names of §4.4 only; an unknown
   gate name is a load error.
3. **Further device models.** Default: the four of §7.3; an `effect` on
   any other device is `FAULT_EFFECT_UNMODELLED`.
4. **Mechanisation of §14.** Default: none; the reference interpreter is
   the oracle.
5. **Memory layout of the opaque C objects.** Default: opaque; only the
   listed functions touch them.
6. **Measurement-based cleanup** (§6.4): the normative fixup, its
   controlled variant and its certificate kind. Default: unitary cleanup
   (`reverse`); `capabilities.mbu` is `false`.
7. **Expansion library** (§11): the gate-level expansion below row
   level. Default: the library `ref` published by `bennett-isa-spec`
   (ripple-carry adders and comparators, linear `inrange` scans,
   one-hot address dispatch, clean scratch released in reverse order);
   a schedule that names no `expansion` binds `ref` at the ISA version
   in the object's header, with the full-library envelope hash published
   for that version in §11.1. [deps: ISA-9.1, ISA-11.1-P3, ISA-11.1-P4]
   For a 0.9 object this is exactly
   `{"name":"ref","version":"0.9","hash":"5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197"}`,
   equally for omission and an explicit binding. [deps: ISA-11.1-P3, ISA-11.1-P4, ISA-11.1]
   §11.1 fixes its schema, ordinals, scratch identities, empty removable
   sets and deterministic decomposition algorithms. [deps: ISA-11.1]
   The bound catalog is published as `spec/ref-0.9.json`. The worked
   `ctl` action fixture (zsw.4) is in
   `conformance/fixtures/controlled-action-09/`: `controlled.bisa`,
   `target.json`, `leaves.json`, `schedule.json`, `frame.json` and
   `certificate.json`. It contains one exact controlled-X leaf, starts
   at time 0 and ends at time 1, with two live fast-class interface wires
   and no workspace. Its README records derivation and the pinned 0.8
   compatibility check separately from the 0.9 bindings.
8. **Enclosure procedure for transcendental entries** (§12.1). Default:
   Taylor series of sin and cos to the first term whose Lagrange
   remainder bound is below 2^−(`precision_bits` + 2), argument reduced
   modulo 2π with an outward-rounded enclosure of π.
9. **Default `epsilon_share`** (§8.1, §11) when a schedule assigns none.
   Default: the exact rational `bindings.epsilon / N`, where N is the
   number of gate operations in the bound-library expansion of one
   invocation of `bindings.region`, including every nested invocation,
   that have no exact native match as defined below. [deps: ISA-8.1, ISA-8.3, ISA-11-P2]
   For this count only, an exact native match is a `gates` entry whose
   opcode, classes, control range and parameters cover the operation
   and whose `epsilon` expression is independent of `eps` and evaluates
   to zero; compute this test before the requested-accuracy filter,
   without selecting an achieved-error entry using the default share. [deps: ISA-8.1, ISA-8.3]
   N counts the gate operations before target scheme expansion and
   includes operations with explicit shares as well as omitted shares;
   the root accuracy is `bindings.epsilon`, not a nested region's
   separately requested accuracy. [deps: ISA-11-P2, ISA-11-P3, ISA-8.2, ISA-8.3]
   Gates with an exact native match take a default share of zero; if
   N=0 all default shares are zero and no division is performed. [deps: ISA-8.1, ISA-8.3]
   The resolved share is represented exactly as a reduced pair (p,q)
   of nonnegative numerator and positive denominator, with zero
   represented by (0,1); it is passed as that rational value to every
   §8.1 comparison, expression and accuracy bucket, without rounding
   to a finite decimal. [deps: ISA-8.1]
   This is a resolved value, not an inserted `epsilon_share` field;
   existing decimal schedule fields and the hashed schedule bytes are
   unchanged by default resolution. [deps: ISA-11-P3, ISA-9.2]
   Explicit shares still supply `eps` by their exact value and the
   §8.1 requested-versus-achieved filter and achieved-error charge
   still apply to every resolved share. [deps: ISA-8.1, ISA-8.3]
   *(non-normative witness)* At `bindings.epsilon: "0.1"`, three gates
   lacking exact native matches give N=3 and default (1,30), even if
   one gate has an explicit share; a fourth, exact-native gate takes
   zero and is excluded from N. [deps: ISA-8.1, ISA-8.3, ISA-11-P2]
   With no such inexact gates N=0. [deps: ISA-8.1, ISA-8.3, ISA-11-P2]
   Omitting expansion on a 0.9 object selects the full-library hash in
   item 7, not the single-qxor witness hash. [deps: ISA-11.1-P3, ISA-11.1-P4]
10. **`any`-class resolution** (§11). Default: the first class in JCS
    order with capacity.
11. **Occupancy rate of a class absent from `rate`** (§8.2). Default: 1.
12. **Classical step timing of CC/R instructions and effects** (§8.2).
    Default: `classical_step_time` each, sequential.
13. **Suite sizes** (§15): the exhaustive widths of suite C and the
    sample counts of `sampled` claims. Default: exhaustive for ≤ 16
    interface bits; 2^16 samples above.
14. **Hardware handling of `qreg.free`** (§3.3). Cleanliness of an
    arbitrary state is not testable nondestructively. Default: on
    hardware the release proceeds without a test and its frame is
    marked unverified, so a segment containing it cannot be uncalled
    (§7.4) and a run containing it is not reverse-eligible (§10);
    releasing a register that was not clean is a program error the
    hardware does not detect *(non-normative: physically its wires are
    then discarded as by an unrecorded measurement; this is a program
    error, not a trace-out operation, §10)*. The same holds for
    `bennett_qreg_prepare` and `bennett_qreg_free` on a non-verifying
    executor. A verifying executor tests and records `FAULT_UB_TRAP` on
    failure (§4.9), or returns `E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN` from the host calls.
15. **Routing and movement cost under a topology** (§8.2–§8.3, §11),
    deferred to 0.10. Default: no routing cost is charged and no routing
    is inserted; a schedule that needs a non-adjacent pair is
    `E_SCHEDULE_INFEASIBLE` naming this item. Absent topology remains
    all-to-all. A producer can supply an explicitly routed gate sequence
    using §4.4 `swap` gates; those gates execute and are charged normally.
    The optional topology schema and adjacency validation are decided in
    0.9; only automatic routing and its movement-cost model are deferred.
16. **Exhaustion of an executor's own classical resources in CC/R**
    (activation stack, history storage; §4.9). CC and R carry no budget
    (§5.4 budgets are Q-tier), so where a finite executor runs out is
    its own limit. Default: a terminal fault record `FAULT_BUDGET_HEAP`
    at the instruction that cannot proceed, raised before any mutation
    by that instruction (§4.9; an executor that cannot guarantee this
    for an exhaustion inside a region call marks the run not
    reverse-eligible); the point is executor-defined and the suites do
    not test it.
17. **Identity-idle step** (§3.6). A variant of the step in which an
    idle step leaves its frame at zero: forward, a = (pc ≠ HALT) into
    clean scratch; dispatch k < n only; rows as printed; the successor
    XORs for k < n and both commit exchanges under a, with no HALT
    successor; then `old_pc ^= HALT` under a (an active frame holds old
    index ⊕ HALT, never 0, since the old index is < n = HALT);
    dispatch uncomputed from old_pc ⊕ HALT under a; a cleared from
    (old_pc ≠ 0). Inverse: a = (old_pc ≠ 0); dispatch from old_pc ⊕
    HALT under a; `old_pc ^= HALT` under a; the two inverse exchanges
    under a; successors and rows undone as printed; dispatch uncomputed
    from pc under a; a cleared from (pc ≠ HALT). Same frame width, same
    F_B and the same postcondition as T2; on pc = HALT with a fresh zero
    frame a forward step is the identity (candidate theorem T7).
    Default: the printed step, whose idle frames record HALT. Hook: an
    expansion library (§11) MAY name this variant as its realisation of
    §3.6, and a schedule binding that library executes and charges it;
    making it the reference changes §3.6 and adds T7.
18. **Checkpointed or pebbled oracle realisations** (§5.2, §5.7, §9.4,
    §11). Default: the full-history reference expansion (B frames, the
    library `ref`). Hook: an expansion library MAY realise §5.2 by
    checkpoints and replay or by pebbling; it MUST list every generated
    allocation, copy, forward evaluation, inverse evaluation and release,
    every repeated evaluation included, with distinct ordinals and
    scratch identities, and carry a full-domain argument that the final
    interface tuple of §5.2 is produced with private scratch clean and
    borrowed correlations restored; a schedule binds its name, version
    and hash; every replay is executed and charged (§8.2); the frame
    descriptor reports the realised history (§9.4); the reference body,
    F_B and the budget unit are unchanged, and T2 remains stated for the
    reference expansion. *(non-normative)* Binary pebbling P_{j+1}(a, b) =
    P_j(a, c); P_j(c, b); P_j(a, c) uses 3^⌈log₂ B⌉ base evaluations and at
    most ⌈log₂ B⌉ intermediate configurations; no polylogarithmic-time
    bound is claimed.

## Version rationale (docs/notes/classical-r-contract-profile.md)

# Classical R-contract publication candidate

The full compatibility identity is **`0.3-r1`**, targeting ISA **`0.9`**.
This is a named profile of the 0.3 draft under §23, not a publication of the
whole draft or a patch to published 0.2.14. The mapping version remains `0.3`:
the change fixes the dialect's consumer contract, not the §16 map. Marker ABI
`0.2`, normaliser `0.2.8` and descriptor version 2 are retained. The candidate
must receive council grading before it can be advertised as accepted.

The normative grading boundary is §1.7, with the profile-specific identities
in §19.9 and §23. Only classical R applicability and its CC launch boundary
are submitted. All other clauses remain ungraded and retain their full
obligations. Quantum R, coherent execution, platform work and mixed native
pointer/container launch contracts are not silently removed or declared inert.

The producer/consumer compatibility tuple is explicit: plugin
`dialect-0.3-r1;isa-0.9`, dialect option/module flag `0.3-r1`, ISA header and ABI
`0.9`, mapping `0.3`, build-record dialect/ISA/replay identities, and checked
ISA 0.9 hashes/certificate bindings. `producer.version` binds the build-record
JCS digest through the existing metadata channel. Published 0.2.14 continues
to identify ISA 0.8 objects. Relabelling an old envelope or retaining its hash
does not migrate it; a selected track requires fresh materialisation and all
dependent identities. No new ISA field is invented.

Typed R faults follow ISA §§4.9/10, not a generic trap: exact effective code,
one terminal record, no values or caller successor, unchanged failing-step
state and the entire reversible prefix preserved. Source-step counters remain
pre-instruction instrumentation, including return boundaries. Tool fuel is
separate. Fault-zero means effective code 4; nonzero program-defined codes
retain all 64 bits. Failed forward execution does not flush or reverse itself.

Console binding preserves §11.2's published close clarification: descriptor
liveness is ordinary reversible runtime memory, while the ISA byte sink stays
available to other descriptors. Normal C main return executes musl exit/stdio
cleanup exactly once, including a final buffer without a newline. No executor
invented flush/close effect is permitted. Tape entries correspond to successful
nonempty write vectors, not printf calls.

The replay identity is **`saved-tape-v1`**, adopting the gate-pinned reference
publication's tool interface (`bennett-isa-spec` at
`c1d13200acb08af4922535f5a15a1ab872b78b41`,
`reference-interpreter/README.md`, “Saved-tape profile v1”). ISA §7.3 explicitly
leaves persisted journal interchange to a versioned replay profile. The saved
journal includes successful effects subsequently cancelled by uncall; the
active ISA tape does not. Replay validates each candidate before commit,
rejects missing/mismatching/trailing input, and never substitutes a source
fault for a replay-validation error. Object, input, entropy, host replies and
budget identities remain separate, mandatory inputs.

The four new corpus groups use the existing 0.3 checker via a small family
registration in the shared runner. They provide clause-retention checks and
finite independent execution evidence: typed fault codes/failed-prefix reset,
version-dependent hashes/stale identity rejection, native formatted bytes and
descriptor-close errors, ISA console atomicity/reset, and valid/corrupt saved
journals. Native C uses the host implementation as an independent byte oracle;
the ISA fixtures are explicitly hand-written boundary programs. Neither is
evidence that the plugin has compiled musl vfprintf, that a production runtime
implements the close wrapper, or that either executor has completed the whole
rung. Those acceptance rows remain with the producer/executor/conformance
owners. Passing `--family r-contract` cannot grade the whole draft.

Council decisions requested: accept the named compatibility identity and
clause boundary; confirm the build-record metadata binding without a new ISA
schema; accept saved-tape-v1 as the profile's replay contract; decide publication
readiness from these finite witnesses and the remaining integration evidence.
No ISA expressibility blocker was found for classical R. If one is identified,
§25.1 must name its exact required change and use `blocked:`, never `reject:`.

````diff
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+/* Independent native byte oracle. A normal main return flushes the last
+ * buffered bytes, which deliberately have no newline. Descriptor 2 is closed
+ * without closing the stdout console sink. These expectations follow POSIX
+ * close/write/writev/lseek and the stated C format, not an executor trace. */
+#include <errno.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <unistd.h>
+#include <sys/uio.h>
+
+int main(void) {
+    struct iovec v = { .iov_base = "x", .iov_len = 1 };
+    if (close(2) != 0) return 1;
+    errno = 0;
+    if (write(2, "x", 1) != -1 || errno != EBADF) return 2;
+    errno = 0;
+    if (writev(2, &v, 1) != -1 || errno != EBADF) return 3;
+    errno = 0;
+    if (lseek(2, 0, SEEK_SET) != -1 || errno != EBADF) return 4;
+    if (printf("%s %d %u %x %c %05d %.3s", "xy", -7, 9u, 42u,
+               'Z', 12, "abcdef") != 22) return 5;
+    return 0;
+}

+
+The full compatibility identity is **`0.3-r1`**, targeting ISA **`0.9`**.
+This is a named profile of the 0.3 draft under §23, not a publication of the
+whole draft or a patch to published 0.2.14. The mapping version remains `0.3`:
+the change fixes the dialect's consumer contract, not the §16 map. Marker ABI
+`0.2`, normaliser `0.2.8` and descriptor version 2 are retained. The candidate
+must receive council grading before it can be advertised as accepted.
+
+The normative grading boundary is §1.7, with the profile-specific identities
+in §19.9 and §23. Only classical R applicability and its CC launch boundary
+are submitted. All other clauses remain ungraded and retain their full
+obligations. Quantum R, coherent execution, platform work and mixed native
+pointer/container launch contracts are not silently removed or declared inert.
+
+The producer/consumer compatibility tuple is explicit: plugin
+`dialect-0.3-r1;isa-0.9`, dialect option/module flag `0.3-r1`, ISA header and ABI
+`0.9`, mapping `0.3`, build-record dialect/ISA/replay identities, and checked
+ISA 0.9 hashes/certificate bindings. `producer.version` binds the build-record
+JCS digest through the existing metadata channel. Published 0.2.14 continues
+to identify ISA 0.8 objects. Relabelling an old envelope or retaining its hash
+does not migrate it; a selected track requires fresh materialisation and all
+dependent identities. No new ISA field is invented.
+
+Typed R faults follow ISA §§4.9/10, not a generic trap: exact effective code,
+one terminal record, no values or caller successor, unchanged failing-step
+state and the entire reversible prefix preserved. Source-step counters remain
+pre-instruction instrumentation, including return boundaries. Tool fuel is
+separate. Fault-zero means effective code 4; nonzero program-defined codes
+retain all 64 bits. Failed forward execution does not flush or reverse itself.
+
+Console binding preserves §11.2's published close clarification: descriptor
+liveness is ordinary reversible runtime memory, while the ISA byte sink stays
+available to other descriptors. Normal C main return executes musl exit/stdio
+cleanup exactly once, including a final buffer without a newline. No executor
+invented flush/close effect is permitted. Tape entries correspond to successful
+nonempty write vectors, not printf calls.
+
+The replay identity is **`saved-tape-v1`**, adopting the gate-pinned reference
+publication's tool interface (`bennett-isa-spec` at
+`c1d13200acb08af4922535f5a15a1ab872b78b41`,
+`reference-interpreter/README.md`, “Saved-tape profile v1”). ISA §7.3 explicitly
+leaves persisted journal interchange to a versioned replay profile. The saved
+journal includes successful effects subsequently cancelled by uncall; the
+active ISA tape does not. Replay validates each candidate before commit,
+rejects missing/mismatching/trailing input, and never substitutes a source
+fault for a replay-validation error. Object, input, entropy, host replies and
+budget identities remain separate, mandatory inputs.
+
+The four new corpus groups use the existing 0.3 checker via a small family
+registration in the shared runner. They provide clause-retention checks and
+finite independent execution evidence: typed fault codes/failed-prefix reset,
+version-dependent hashes/stale identity rejection, native formatted bytes and
+descriptor-close errors, ISA console atomicity/reset, and valid/corrupt saved
+journals. Native C uses the host implementation as an independent byte oracle;
+the ISA fixtures are explicitly hand-written boundary programs. Neither is
+evidence that the plugin has compiled musl vfprintf, that a production runtime
+implements the close wrapper, or that either executor has completed the whole
+rung. Those acceptance rows remain with the producer/executor/conformance
+owners. Passing `--family r-contract` cannot grade the whole draft.
+
+Council decisions requested: accept the named compatibility identity and
+clause boundary; confirm the build-record metadata binding without a new ISA
+schema; accept saved-tape-v1 as the profile's replay contract; decide publication
+readiness from these finite witnesses and the remaining integration evidence.
+No ISA expressibility blocker was found for classical R. If one is identified,
+§25.1 must name its exact required change and use `blocked:`, never `reject:`.

diff --git a/scripts/dialect_r_contract.py b/scripts/dialect_r_contract.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1c14172
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/dialect_r_contract.py
@@ -0,0 +1,192 @@
+"""Finite R-profile contract vectors; execution comes from the pinned ISA reader.
+
+Clause checks establish retention only. Native printf is an independent byte
+oracle; the hand-written ISA fixtures do not claim plugin/musl integration.
+"""
+import json
+import re
+import subprocess
+
+import dialect_check as d
+import dialect_check_v02 as v2
+import dialect_cc as cc
+from dialect_profile import ISA08, profile, using_profile
+
+CASES = d.ROOT / 'corpus' / 'legality' / 'r-contract'
+# ISA reference CLI output schema (U): larger integers use decimal strings.
+JSON_EXACT_INTEGER_MAX = (1 << 53) - 1
+
+
+def clauses(runner, case):
+    for section, sentence in case['requires']:
+        heading = re.search(r'^###? ' + re.escape(section) + r'\.? ', runner.spec, re.M)
+        if heading is None:
+            raise d.Fail('missing R-contract section ' + section)
+        end = re.search(r'^###? ', runner.spec[heading.end():], re.M)
+        text = runner.spec[heading.end():heading.end() + end.start()] if end else runner.spec[heading.end():]
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'clause in §' + section, True,
+                 ' '.join(sentence.split()) in ' '.join(text.split()))
+
+
+def object_file(runner, case, suffix='', functions=None):
+    path = runner.tmp / (case['id'] + suffix + '.bisa')
+    cc.emit(runner, path, functions if functions is not None else case['functions'],
+            case['signatures'], {k: bytes.fromhex(v) for k, v in case.get('data', {}).items()},
+            case.get('devices'))
+    return path
+
+
+def observations(case, got, expected):
+    for key, value in expected.items():
+        v2.equal(case['id'], key, value, got[key])
+
+
+def faults(runner, case):
+    for code in case['codes']:
+        path = object_file(runner, case, '-' + str(code),
+                           [body.replace('fault 2', 'fault ' + str(code)) for body in case['functions']])
+        got = runner.isa.call('run-cc', path, 'main')
+        effective = code if code else 4
+        encoded = str(effective) if effective > JSON_EXACT_INTEGER_MAX else effective
+        observations(case, got, dict(case['expected'], fault=encoded))
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'one terminal record', 1, len(got['faults']))
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'exact terminal record code', encoded, got['faults'][0]['code'])
+        reset = runner.isa.call('reverse', path, 'main')
+        observations(case, reset, case['reset'])
+    # A generic trap is a distinguishable, incorrect lowering of fault 2.
+    path = object_file(runner, case, '-trap', [body.replace('fault 2', 'trap') for body in case['functions']])
+    got = runner.isa.call('run-cc', path, 'main')
+    v2.equal(case['id'], 'trap has only code 4', 4, got['fault'])
+    v2.equal(case['id'], 'trap cannot implement fault 2', False, got['fault'] == 2)
+    # Retain the independent 0/1/2 source-step boundary witness in this family.
+    runner.state_check(runner, runner.block('state', 'r-budget-prefix'))
+
+
+def identity(runner, case):
+    current = object_file(runner, case)
+    new_hash = runner.isa.call('hash', current)['symbols']['main']['interface_hash']
+    with using_profile(ISA08):
+        legacy_case = dict(case, signatures={'main': cc.signature([], [])})
+        legacy = object_file(runner, legacy_case, '-legacy')
+    old_hash = runner.isa.call('hash', legacy)['symbols']['main']['interface_hash']
+    v2.equal(case['id'], 'ISA version changes semantic envelope hash', False, old_hash == new_hash)
+    # Put the old claimed hash on real 0.9 bytes. A version-label rewrite is insufficient.
+    stale = runner.tmp / 'stale-identity.bisa'
+    stale.write_text(current.read_text().replace(new_hash, old_hash))
+    reject(runner, stale, 'check', [], 'hash')
+    # A mismatched ABI is also rejected, independently of the claimed hash.
+    stale.write_text(current.read_text().replace('"abi":"0.9"', '"abi":"0.8"'))
+    reject(runner, stale, 'check', [], 'abi')
+
+
+def reject(runner, path, verb, options, diagnostic):
+    runner.isa.build()
+    result = subprocess.run([runner.isa.exe, verb, path, *options], capture_output=True,
+                            text=True, env=v2.headless_env(), timeout=30)
+    v2.equal(path.name, 'diagnostic exit', 1, result.returncode)
+    v2.equal(path.name, 'no success JSON', '', result.stdout)
+    if diagnostic.lower() not in result.stderr.lower():
+        raise d.Fail(path.name + ': expected diagnostic ' + diagnostic + '; actual ' + result.stderr)
+
+
+def console(runner, case):
+    source = CASES / case['native']
+    for major in ('18', '23'):
+        exe = runner.tmp / ('console-native-' + major)
+        v2.command([runner.frontends[major] / 'clang', '-O2', '-fno-builtin', source, '-o', exe])
+        result = subprocess.run([exe], capture_output=True, env=v2.headless_env(), timeout=10)
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'native status LLVM ' + major, 0, result.returncode)
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'native formatted bytes LLVM ' + major, case['expected']['console_hex'], result.stdout.hex())
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'native stderr LLVM ' + major, b'', result.stderr)
+    path = object_file(runner, case)
+    observations(case, runner.isa.call('run-cc', path, 'main'), case['expected'])
+    observations(case, runner.isa.call('reverse', path, 'main'), case['reset'])
+    bad = object_file(runner, case, '-bad-range', [body.replace('const.i64 4096', 'const.i64 0') for body in case['functions']])
+    observations(case, runner.isa.call('run-cc', bad, 'main'), case['invalid_range'])
+
+
+def record_and_replay(runner, case, path, saved):
+    forward = runner.isa.call('run-cc', path, 'main', '--tape-out', saved)
+    observations(case, forward, case['expected'])
+    journal = json.loads(saved.read_text())
+    v2.equal(case['id'], 'saved journal schema and hand-derived bytes', case['journal'], journal)
+    for verb in ('run-cc', 'reverse'):
+        plain = runner.isa.call(verb, path, 'main')
+        replay = runner.isa.call(verb, path, 'main', '--replay-tape', saved)
+        v2.equal(case['id'], verb + ' replay exact report', plain, replay)
+
+
+def replay_cancelled_effects(runner, case):
+    # A cancelled effect belongs to the saved journal, not the active tape.
+    cancelled_case = dict(case, signatures={'main': cc.signature([], []), 'writer': cc.signature([], [])})
+    cancelled = object_file(runner, cancelled_case, '-cancelled', [
+        'fn r @main () () () () ()\n^entry():\ncall @writer\nuncall @writer () ()\nfault 3',
+        case['functions'][0].replace('@main', '@writer')])
+    cancelled_saved = runner.tmp / 'cancelled-journal.json'
+    failed = runner.isa.call('run-cc', cancelled, 'main', '--tape-out', cancelled_saved)
+    observations(case, failed, dict(status='FAILED', fault=3, results=[], console_hex='', effect_tape_length=0))
+    v2.equal(case['id'], 'cancelled forward effect retained', case['journal'], json.loads(cancelled_saved.read_text()))
+    v2.equal(case['id'], 'FAILED cancelled replay', failed,
+             runner.isa.call('run-cc', cancelled, 'main', '--replay-tape', cancelled_saved))
+    observations(case, runner.isa.call('reverse', cancelled, 'main', '--replay-tape', cancelled_saved),
+                 dict(status='REVERSED', console_hex='', effect_tape_length=0, memory_equals_entry=True))
+
+
+def reject_corrupt_tapes(runner, case, path, saved):
+    for mutation in case['corruptions']:
+        entries = json.loads(saved.read_text())
+        if mutation == 'missing':
+            entries.pop()
+        elif mutation == 'trailing':
+            entries.append(entries[0])
+        elif mutation == 'reordered':
+            entries.reverse()
+        else:
+            entries[0][mutation] = case['corruptions'][mutation]
+        corrupt = runner.tmp / ('corrupt-' + mutation + '.json')
+        corrupt.write_text(json.dumps(entries))
+        out = runner.tmp / ('rejected-' + mutation + '.json')
+        reject(runner, path, 'run-cc', ['main', '--replay-tape', str(corrupt), '--tape-out', str(out)], 'replay mismatch')
+        v2.equal(case['id'], 'corrupt replay writes no tape', False, out.exists())
+    malformed = runner.tmp / 'malformed-tape.json'
+    malformed.write_text('[{"dev":"console","dev":"console","op":"write","args":[4096,1],"bytes":"78"}]')
+    reject(runner, path, 'run-cc', ['main', '--replay-tape', str(malformed)], 'duplicate')
+
+
+def tape(runner, case):
+    path = object_file(runner, case)
+    saved = runner.tmp / (case['id'] + '.json')
+    record_and_replay(runner, case, path, saved)
+    replay_cancelled_effects(runner, case)
+    reject_corrupt_tapes(runner, case, path, saved)
+
+
+CHECKS = {'faults': faults, 'identity': identity, 'console': console, 'tape': tape}
+
+
+def check_case(runner, case):
+    clauses(runner, case)
+    CHECKS[case['kind']](runner, case)
+    return {'claim': 'clause retention and finite independent native/ISA boundary vectors; not whole-program producer conformance',
+            'case': case['id']}
+
+
+def check_all(runner):
+    if runner.selected and 'r-contract' not in runner.selected:
+        return
+    cases = [json.loads(path.read_text()) for path in sorted(CASES.glob('*.json'))]
+    v2.equal('r-contract', 'one case group per contract kind', sorted(CHECKS), sorted(c['kind'] for c in cases))
+    for case in cases:
+        runner.check('r-contract', case['id'], case['rule'], lambda case=case: check_case(runner, case))
+
+
+def check_runtime_contracts(runner):
+    from dialect_0214 import check_all as check_delivery
+    check_delivery(runner)
+    if profile().isa == '0.9':
+        check_all(runner)
+
+
+def require_legacy_families(parser, selected):
+    if 'r-contract' in selected:
+        parser.error('r-contract requires tools/dialect_check_v03.py (ISA 0.9)')
diff --git a/scripts/test_dialect_r_contract.py b/scripts/test_dialect_r_contract.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bfa3853
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/test_dialect_r_contract.py
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+"""Soundness of the R-contract clause/fixture registration, without an executor."""
+import json
+import contextlib
+import io
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import dialect_check as d
+import dialect_r_contract as contract
+import dialect_check_v02 as v2
+
+
+class ContractClauses(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_each_case_detects_removal_of_its_binding_clause(self):
+        text = (d.ROOT / 'spec' / 'Bennett-Dialect-Spec-0.3-draft.md').read_text()
+        for path in sorted(contract.CASES.glob('*.json')):
+            case = json.loads(path.read_text())
+            with self.subTest(case=case['id']):
+                contract.clauses(SimpleNamespace(spec=text), case)
+                sentence = case['requires'][0][1]
+                self.assertIn(sentence, text)
+                with self.assertRaises(d.Fail):
+                    contract.clauses(SimpleNamespace(spec=text.replace(sentence, '', 1)), case)
+
+    def test_a_clause_in_the_wrong_section_does_not_count(self):
+        text = '### 11.2 Console\nTyped fault required.\n### 17.6 R tier\nNo rule here.\n'
+        case = {'id': 'misplaced', 'requires': [['17.6', 'Typed fault required.']]}
+        with self.assertRaises(d.Fail):
+            contract.clauses(SimpleNamespace(spec=text), case)
+
+    def test_a_missing_case_group_fails_instead_of_empty_green(self):
+        with patch.object(contract, 'CASES') as cases:
+            cases.glob.return_value = []
+            with self.assertRaises(d.Fail):
+                contract.check_all(SimpleNamespace(selected={'r-contract'}))
+
+    def test_legacy_checker_cannot_report_empty_green_for_this_family(self):
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
+            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as caught:
+                v2.main(['--family', 'r-contract'])
+        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, 2)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

@@ -1,13 +1,14 @@

-candidate. It derives from draft 0.2.12 (accepted by the sol seat in round 11) and carries the

+profile `0.3-r1` (§1.7) is an acceptance candidate for separate council grading, not an
+assertion of council acceptance or whole-0.3 conformance. It derives from draft 0.2.12 (accepted by the sol seat in round 11) and carries the
 matching 0.2.13 allocator/PPC amendments and the 0.2.14 runtime integer instance delivery and console close clarification published in `Bennett-Dialect-Spec.md`. The grading target is Bennett ISA **0.9** (`Bennett-ISA-Spec-0.9.md`, accepted by all three
 seats, K1–K81). The dossier is `docs/notes/2026-11-01-dialect-0.3-dossier.md`.
 
 **Versioning.** Dialect 0.3: markers 0.2, handles 0.3, regions 0.3, oracle-abi 0.3, tdl 0.3, effects 0.3, norm 0.2.8, map 0.3, asm 0.2, platform 0.3, driver 0.3, corpus 0.2; targets ISA 0.9. [deps: DLT-front-P2, DLT-23]

+Marker signatures, the header and descriptor version 2 are unchanged from 0.2.12; every reference object and hash changes with the ISA version string (ISA §9.2). Producers and executors of the published 0.2.x/ISA 0.8 track stay on that track until they migrate explicitly. @@ -178,6 +179,53 @@ A module's **verdict** is one of:
 A module that would be rejected and blocked is rejected. Warnings (`BD-W-*`, §22.4) never change
 a verdict.
 
+### 1.7 Classical R-contract profile (acceptance candidate)
+
+`0.3-r1` names a full dialect compatibility identity under §23 for the classical
+R-contract slice of this draft targeting ISA 0.9. It is not an alias for `0.3`, a
+0.2.x patch, or a claim that the rest of 0.3 has been graded. Its publication is
+conditional on council acceptance of this slice; until then it is a candidate.
+The following is the exact grading boundary, restricted to each clause's
+classical R applicability and the CC launch stub that enters it:
+
+| Sections submitted | Contract carried by the slice |
+|---|---|
+| §§1–5 | conformance, diagnostics, ordinary marker ABI/recognition, processing order, placement, addresses and device-closure analysis |
+| §§7.1, 7.5(b), 7.6; §§9.1–9.5 | R entry/outlining, measure prohibition, budget resolution, units and exhaustion |
+| §§11.1–11.2, 11.4–11.5; §12 | R devices, CC launch services, typed faults, complete applicable normalisation and residual validation |
+| §§13–15 | arithmetic, calls/recursion, varargs, stack/control transfer, exit and asm/intrinsic realisation in classical R |
+| §§16.1–16.5; §17 | materialised mapping/identity obligations, layout, classical memory, shadow stack, lowering, faults, counters and native comparison |
+| §§18.1, 18.6–18.7; §§19.1–19.2, 19.4–19.9 | classical reference state, reversal/replay, outcome comparison, linked closure/process lifecycle, launch, layout and output identities |

+**R-contract console binding.** The `console` entry in `devices.models` is
+`{"version":"0.9"}`. Its state is the initially empty byte sequence of ISA
+§7.3, shared by stdout and stderr in effect order; it preserves all bytes,
+including NUL, without encoding or newline conversion. A successful nonempty
+write appends exactly its bytes and one tape entry; invalid memory faults 7
+before appending any byte or entry. There is no ISA flush or close operation.
+Buffering, descriptor liveness, errno and exit handlers are ordinary linked
+musl/runtime memory and code, charged and reversed with that code. Closing fd 1
+does not close fd 2 or the console device; the EBADF rule above takes precedence
+over ESPIPE on a closed descriptor. A failed syscall that returns errno without
+an effect adds no device record.

+Return-time flushing MUST emit buffered bytes even without a trailing newline, with no added newline or close record.

+cleanup path as explicit `exit`, exactly once, before successful status return.
+`_Exit` bypasses cleanup, and a terminal fault executes neither cleanup nor a
+caller successor. The executor executes emitted code/effects; it MUST NOT
+invent a return-time flush, a host print, or a host-side close. Whole-run
+reversal restores buffer contents, descriptor liveness and console state as
+well as memory and tape. The source-level printf call count is not the tape
+length: actual successful nonempty write vectors determine the tape entries.

+**R-contract saved replay (tool contract, not an ISA envelope extension).**
+The R-contract replay profile is `saved-tape-v1`.
+This profile adopts the saved-tape profile v1 of the ISA reference-interpreter
+tool interface. ISA §7.3, §10 still own the active tape: ordered `(dev, op, args)`
+entries, with launch iterator operands unsigned 64-bit little-endian, in ISA
+operand order and pointers zero-extended from `ptr_width`. Device history also
+retains the reversal data of ISA §7.3. The saved file is an execution journal:
+every successfully executed effect in execution order, including effects later
+cancelled by segment `uncall`; a faulting effect contributes nothing. Whole-run
+reversal empties the active tape but MUST NOT erase the saved forward journal.
+
+The journal is a JSON array. Each entry has exactly `args`, `bytes`, `dev`, `op`,
+with no duplicate or extra keys. `dev`/`op` are strings; `args` is an array of
+canonical unsigned integers fitting u128, encoded as JSON numbers through
+2^53−1 and decimal strings above it, without signs, leading zeros, fractions
+or exponents. `bytes` is even-length hex (empty allowed); readers accept either
+case, writers use lowercase. Writers use canonical JSON followed by LF. The
+u128 tool encoding does not widen any ISA operand. `bytes` contains the bytes
+transferred by that operation, not its undo data: console output, bytes written
+by clock/entropy/block reads, or block-write input, as appropriate.
+
+`run-cc`, CC/R `reverse`, and `run-program` MUST support `--tape-out <file>`
+and `--replay-tape <file>`, each at most once, and allow both together. Tape-out
+saves the forward journal after command success, including a normal JSON
+`FAILED` outcome; reverse with an explicit prefix length saves only that
+forward prefix. Replay and reversal errors write no tape output.
+Replay requires the same object/root, entry, arguments, entry memory/global
+images, entropy, checked host-request replies, measurement inputs when
+applicable, source budgets, tool fuel and forward prefix length. The build
+record (§19.9) identifies the replay profile; a saved journal is not a
+substitute for these inputs, a certificate, or object/entry identity checks.
+
+Before committing each effect the executor compares the next saved entry's
+device, operation, integer operands and transferred bytes with the deterministic
+candidate formed from the current state. Mismatch or missing input MUST leave
+that step's memory, devices, history and journal cursor unchanged; earlier
+successfully committed steps remain a prefix. Unconsumed entries at the end
+of the requested forward run/prefix also fail. An exact-match journal produces
+byte-identical stdout JSON for the same command and inputs, including results,
+faults, console, active tape and reset report, without replay-only fields.
+Changed payload/operand/device/op, deletion, insertion, reordering, malformed
+schema/hex/integer encodings and I/O errors MUST fail loudly. A replay mismatch
+exits 1 with a `replay mismatch` diagnostic citing ISA §7.3, §10, no success JSON
+and no tape-output write. It MUST NOT be converted into `FAILED` with a
+fabricated source fault code. Schema and I/O failures are likewise tool errors.
+The active tape and the saved journal coincide only when no effect was
+cancelled; consumers MUST use tape-out rather than save the active array when
+there was cancellation. No persistence/import of private undo frames is implied.
````
